articles.title: Metrô de SP encerra uso de bilhete magnético após mais de 50 anos | G1
articles.standfirst: Passageiros que ainda possuírem o modelo podem utilizá-lo nas catracas até este sábado (31); depois disso, os bilhetes poderão ser trocados por QR Codes nas bilheterias das estações Paraíso e Tatuapé, das 6h às 22h.
articles.summary: Passageiros que ainda possuírem o modelo podem utilizá-lo nas catracas até este sábado (31); depois disso, os bilhetes poderão ser trocados por QR Codes nas bilheterias das estações Paraíso e Tatuapé, das 6h às 22h.
articles.body:
Metrô de SP encerra bilhete magnético após mais de 50 anos — Foto: Divulgação/Metrô SP

O bilhete magnético do tipo Edmonson, utilizado para acesso às estações do Metrô desde o começo da operação comercial do sistema, em 1974, vai deixar de ser aceito nas catracas das estações a partir deste domingo (1°) . Com isso, a utilização dos bilhetes pode ser feita nas catracas das linhas 1-Azul, 2-Verde, 3-Vermelha e 15-Prata até este sábado (31).

Segundo o Metrô, estima-se que 1 milhão de bilhetes magnéticos devam estar nas mãos dos passageiros. Com isso, de 1º de novembro a 31 de janeiro de 2027, as pessoas que ainda tiverem esse meio de acesso poderão trocá-los por QR Codes nas estações Paraíso e Tatuapé.

A medida marca a transição das formas de pagamento para os meios digitais, eletrônicos e por aproximação disponíveis no sistema.

Os passageiros que ainda tiverem os bilhetes magnéticos poderão se dirigir às bilheterias das estações Paraíso, nas linhas 1-Azul e 2-Verde, e Tatuapé, na linha 3-Vermelha, das 6h às 22h, para realizarem a troca por QR Codes. Os bilhetes magnéticos deverão estar válidos e em boas condições de conservação.

As pessoas que tiverem até 10 bilhetes poderão realizar a troca no mesmo instante da solicitação. Aqueles que tiverem acima desse montante deverão entregá-los para análise e validação, apresentando o documento de identificação e fornecendo um endereço de e-mail ou telefone para contato após o procedimento. Após averiguação, o passageiro será informado sobre a data de retirada dos QR Codes.

Com o fim da circulação dos bilhetes magnéticos, os passageiros poderão pagar as passagens com Bilhete Único, cartão TOP e os bilhetes unitários com QR Code, sejam eles impressos ou digitais.

As pessoas poderão também realizar o pagamento nas catracas, utilizando cartões físicos ou virtuais de crédito e débito das bandeiras Elo, Mastercard e Visa .

Metrô de SP passa a aceitar cartão de crédito e débito na catraca — Foto: Fernando Frazão/Agência Brasil

Além da dificuldade de manutenção dos equipamentos de leitura, a produção e a distribuição dos bilhetes magnéticos envolvem uma estrutura considerada mais complexa.

De acordo com o Metrô, os cartões precisam passar por etapas de fabricação especializada, transporte, armazenamento seguro, distribuição para as estações e reposição dos estoques.

Também existem custos relacionados a logística, armazenamento, transporte, controle de estoque, recolhimento e manutenção dos equipamentos utilizados para a leitura dos bilhetes.

Bilhete faz parte da história do Metrô de São Paulo

Apesar de estar sendo substituído , o bilhete magnético se tornou um dos símbolos da história do transporte metroviário de São Paulo.

O modelo acompanha o sistema desde 1974, quando o Metrô iniciou suas operações comerciais. Durante décadas, o pequeno papel-cartão com tarja magnética foi utilizado por milhões de passageiros em deslocamentos para o trabalho, a escola e outros compromissos pela cidade.

Para o Metrô, o bilhete também passou a fazer parte da memória afetiva dos paulistanos e de diferentes gerações que utilizaram o sistema.

O modelo se soma a outros objetos que marcaram diferentes períodos da evolução tecnológica, como fichas telefônicas, orelhões e relógios analógicos das plataformas.

O nome do modelo utilizado pelo Metrô tem origem em Thomas Edmondson, chefe de estação da Newcastle and Carlisle Railway, na Inglaterra.

A partir de 1839, Edmondson desenvolveu um sistema padronizado de emissão de passagens ferroviárias. A tecnologia substituiu os antigos bilhetes manuscritos por cartões previamente impressos e numerados.

Os bilhetes eram validados no momento da venda, permitindo mais controle da operação e das receitas das ferrovias. O sistema acabou sendo adotado por empresas ferroviárias de diferentes países.

Mais de um século depois, o modelo chegou ao Metrô de São Paulo. Quando o sistema começou a funcionar comercialmente, em 1974, os bilhetes em papel-cartão com tarja magnética eram considerados uma tecnologia moderna.

Agora, após mais de cinco décadas de uso, o sistema será definitivamente descontinuado.

articles.title: Meet Grace De Souza, the 13-year-old from Goa who spent her summer break turning the moringa trees in her family’s backyard into a homemade powder business, watering plants at sunrise and serving customers from home
articles.summary: For most children, summer vacations are a time to sleep a little longer, spend hours playing with friends and take a break from schoolwork.
articles.body: For most children, summer vacations are a time to sleep a little longer, spend hours playing with friends and take a break from schoolwork. But for 13-year-old Grace de Souza from Goa, the holidays brought an entirely different routine. Her mornings began with watering plants, followed by hours of carefully sorting, drying and processing leaves. By the time the work was complete, the teenager had turned something growing in her family's backyard into a product that people were willing to pay for.What makes her initiative particularly interesting is that it did not begin with an elaborate business plan or a desire to make money. It started with a simple observation: her family had moringa trees at home, but many other households did not. Grace wondered if she could make the leaves available to people who wanted to include them in their everyday food.The idea eventually became her own small summer venture, producing and selling homemade moringa powder.How Grace turned two backyard trees into a small businessGrace lives in Moira, Goa, and is a Class 9 student at St Mary's Convent High School in Mapusa. She began making moringa powder on May 1, 2026, using leaves harvested from the two moringa trees in her family's garden, as per a report by The Better India.Her interest in the plant developed gradually. Moringa was already a familiar ingredient in the de Souza household. Her mother, Maria de Mello, regularly incorporated its leaves into dal, soups, khichdi, rice and even smoothies for Grace's baby brother.Growing up, Grace had also watched her mother prepare homemade products for customers. Maria runs a small home-based venture called The Goan Homestead, which sells pickles, jams, masalas, coconut oil, handmade soaps and ready-to-eat food.Grace often sat beside her mother, observing how different products were prepared. Sometimes, she helped pack orders or stick labels on products."I used to sit beside my mother and watch everything she made. Sometimes I would help her pack products or stick labels, and sometimes I would just sit quietly and watch because I found it interesting," Grace told the outlet.Over time, watching her mother work seems to have made the idea of creating something of her own feel natural."We are lucky because we have two moringa trees in our garden. But many people don't. I thought maybe I could make the powder so it becomes easier for them to use it," she said.Her mother, meanwhile, was surprised by how quickly Grace moved from an idea to action."This was completely her idea," Maria told The Better India, recalling how her daughter wanted to make moringa powder for people who did not have the trees growing at home.The three-to-four-day process behind every packetMaking the powder is not as simple as plucking a few leaves and grinding them. Grace follows a careful process that takes around three to four days to complete.She first harvests fresh leaves from the trees and separates the tiny leaves from their stems, one by one. The leaves are then spread across trays and kept in the sun for a day.After this, they are brought indoors for another two to three days of shade drying. Grace checks them regularly, turning the leaves so that they dry evenly."Every hour I go back to check the leaves because the top layer dries quickly while the leaves underneath remain fresh, so I keep turning them properly to make sure everything dries evenly," she explained.She is also particular about hygiene. The trays are kept in a clean, open space, away from animals and falling leaves. Once the leaves become sufficiently crisp, they are ground into a fine powder using a regular mixer grinder. Her parents help her seal the finished product into packets.One detail that surprised her was how much the leaves shrink during the process. According to Grace, one kilogram of fresh leaves produces only around 250 grams of powder.Each 100-gram packet is sold for Rs 150.From 20 packets to nearly Rs 3,000 in earningsIn just over a month of starting the venture, Grace had sold approximately 20 packets and earned close to Rs 3,000.The customers are largely people who already visit her family's home to purchase products from The Goan Homestead. Many notice the green moringa powder displayed alongside the other homemade products and enquire about it.Her earnings are currently being saved. Her mother allows her to keep the money she makes from selling the powder, giving her an opportunity to understand the value of the work that goes into earning it.The family has also started planting more moringa saplings as interest in the powder increases.A summer routine that begins at sunriseWhile the small venture has given Grace an opportunity to earn, it has also become part of her everyday responsibilities.Her mornings begin with watering the garden before the sun gets too hot. She also helps look after her one-year-old brother while her mother manages customer orders and the family's home business.When customers visit, Grace helps her mother attend to them. Between household responsibilities and making the powder, her summer break has become a combination of gardening, learning and work.Importantly, she does not want to stop once school reopens. Grace told The Better India that she hopes to continue making moringa powder alongside her studies and may eventually experiment with other products.Her mother believes that such experiences teach children to understand the value of effort and responsibility. For Grace, however, the experience appears to be about more than earning money.She has discovered that an idea does not always need a big investment or a complicated plan to take shape. Sometimes, it can begin with something growing quietly in the backyard. And for this 13-year-old from Goa, two moringa trees were enough to get started.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: In 2006, an Italian father living in England excluded two men from his will, denying they were his sons; 20 years later, an English court has allowed only €46,110 of a €381,796 Italian inheritance judgment to be registered
articles.summary: A family inheritance dispute that began with a father's decision to exclude two men from his will has returned to an English court nearly two decades
articles.body: A family inheritance dispute that began with a father's decision to exclude two men from his will has returned to an English court nearly two decades later. The case involved two men who claimed to be the sons of an Italian man living in England, Davide Sidoli, but were denied a share of his estate after he rejected their claims of paternity. Although Italian courts later recognised them as his sons and awarded them a combined inheritance of more than €381,000, an English court has now ruled that only a small part of that amount can be registered for enforcement in England.In a judgment dated October 29, 2026, in Antonio Sidoli and Another v Dante Sidoli and Others ([2026] EWHC 2769 (BP)), the High Court of Justice, Business and Property Courts of England and Wales, examined whether an Italian inheritance judgment could be enforced against relatives living in England. According to the judgment available in The National Archives, Mr Justice Thompsell allowed the registration of €46,110.07, plus applicable interest, but refused to recognise the Italian ruling to the extent that it dealt with assets situated in England. The decision turned on the limits of foreign courts' jurisdiction over inheritance matters involving property in another country.How the inheritance dispute beganDavide Sidoli died on September 14, 2006, after making a will dated August 22 that year. In the document, he left his estate to his brother Dante Sidoli and Dante's wife, Anna Moruzzi. He specifically excluded his former wife's two sons, Antonio and Andrea Sidoli, stating that he did not consider them his biological children and therefore did not believe he had a moral obligation to leave them anything.Antonio and Andrea challenged this decision, maintaining that Davide was their father. The dispute also involved the earlier estate of Davide's father, Quintilio Sidoli, who had died in 2004 and had left property and other assets to Davide. Both Davide and Quintilio were Italian citizens but were domiciled in England when they died.The two men began legal proceedings in Italy in 2012. On February 21, 2020, a court in Piacenza accepted their claim of paternity, declared them legitimate heirs and set aside the relevant provisions of Davide's will. It awarded them €381,796.31, along with legal interest and other relief. Dante and Anna challenged the decision, but the Court of Appeal of Bologna dismissed their appeal on December 28, 2022.Why the case reached an English courtAlthough Antonio and Andrea had secured a favourable ruling in Italy, they still needed to establish that it could be enforced against the respondents in England. They therefore approached the English courts under the Foreign Judgments (Reciprocal Enforcement) Act 1933. Their initial attempt to register the Italian judgment was challenged. An earlier registration order was cancelled after the respondents applied to have it set aside. In June 2025, Deputy Master Dew refused the application, finding that the Italian courts did not have jurisdiction to determine the succession to the estate of someone domiciled in England.Antonio and Andrea appealed that decision. Their argument was that the Italian courts had the authority to decide inheritance matters concerning assets located in Italy, even if the wider estate included property in England. The respondents, meanwhile, argued that the Italian judgment should not be enforced because it had attempted to invalidate an English will and determine the inheritance of assets belonging to a person domiciled in England.Court separates Italian and English propertyMr Justice Thompsell examined the different parts of the Italian ruling rather than treating it as one indivisible decision. He explained that English law could recognise the jurisdiction of Italian courts over property situated in Italy, but not their authority to decide the validity of an English will or determine succession to assets located in England. The judge also considered the principle of reciprocal enforcement, under which foreign judgments can be recognised when the relevant legal requirements are met. He noted that the Italian courts' authority over inheritance matters did not automatically extend to property outside Italy.As a result, the judge partly allowed the appeal. He ruled that the Italian judgment could be registered insofar as it concerned the succession to Italian property belonging to Quintilio and Davide. However, the parts relating to Davide's English estate and the validity of his English will could not be enforced through this route.How the court arrived at €46,110The court then worked out how much of the original award related to property that the Italian courts had authority to deal with. It calculated the value of Davide's Italian estate, including the inheritance he had received from Quintilio, at €410,855.93. The Italian inheritance rules allowed Antonio and Andrea to claim a combined two-thirds share of Davide's estate, calculated at €273,923.95.The value of the relevant Italian immovable property transferred, or to be transferred, to Antonio and Andrea was much lower, at €45,865.79. The judge used this figure to determine the proportion of the inheritance award that could be registered in England. He also added €244.28 towards the appeal costs, bringing the total to €46,110.07. Applicable Italian statutory interest from February 21, 2020, will also be added to this amount.The judgment does not resolve the wider family dispute or determine the ownership of Davide's English assets. Instead, it establishes how much of the Italian inheritance ruling can be recognised for enforcement in England. Nearly 20 years after Davide's death, Antonio and Andrea have secured recognition of part of their inheritance claim, while the larger portion of the Italian award cannot be enforced in England through this registration.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2019, a Florida homeowner disputed her insurer's water-damage payment; Supreme Court ruled a later notice law could not apply retroactively
articles.summary: A Florida homeowner’s dispute over a water-damage payment has clarified when a state law requiring notice before suing a property insurer applies.
articles.body: A Florida homeowner’s dispute over a water-damage payment has clarified when a state law requiring notice before suing a property insurer applies. On October 22, 2026, the Florida Supreme Court ruled that the presuit-notice requirement introduced in 2021 cannot be applied retroactively to property insurance policies issued before the law took effect. The case involved Rebecca Hughes, whose homeowners policy with Universal Property & Casualty Insurance Company ran from April 24, 2019, to April 24, 2020. After disputing the insurer’s payment for water damage, Hughes sued in August 2021 without giving the notice required under the new law. The trial court dismissed her complaint, but the Sixth District Court of Appeal reversed. In Universal Property & Casualty Insurance Company v. Rebecca Hughes, No. SC2024-0025 (Fla. Oct. 22, 2026), the Supreme Court approved the Sixth District’s decision and rejected a conflicting ruling from the Fourth District. All 7 justices agreed with the outcome, with Justice Tanenbaum writing a separate concurring opinion.Florida water-damage claim dispute: How the Rebecca Hughes case reached the Supreme CourtHughes held a homeowners insurance policy with Universal from April 24, 2019, to April 24, 2020. On May 29, 2019, she filed a claim for water damage. Universal reviewed the claim and made a payment, but Hughes considered the amount insufficient. She obtained 3 repair bids and sought additional payment from the insurer, according to the Florida Supreme Court’s opinion. On July 1, 2021, section 627.70152 of the Florida Statutes took effect as part of a broader overhaul of property insurance law. The statute covers lawsuits arising under residential or commercial property insurance policies, subject to its terms and exceptions. It introduced a requirement for claimants to give the Florida Department of Financial Services written notice of their intention to sue at least 10 business days before filing a lawsuit. Under subsection (5), a court must dismiss without prejudice a suit involving a claim for which the required notice was not given. A dismissal without prejudice does not, by itself, prevent the claimant from bringing the case again.On August 4, 2021, Hughes sued Universal over the disputed payment without submitting the new notice. Universal asked the trial court to dismiss her complaint, arguing that the notice requirement applied. The trial court agreed and dismissed the case without prejudice. Hughes appealed, and Florida’s Sixth District Court of Appeal reversed the dismissal. The dispute reached the state’s highest court to resolve a conflict among the district appeals courts over whether the new requirement applied to policies issued before July 1, 2021.In Cole v. Universal Property & Casualty Insurance Co., 363 So. 3d 1089 (Fla. 4th DCA 2023), the Fourth District had concluded that the notice requirement applied retroactively to existing policies. The Third District later adopted that interpretation in a separate case, while the First, Second, Fifth and Sixth Districts concluded that the statute did not apply retroactively. The Supreme Court heard oral arguments in Hughes’s case on February 5, 2025. The recording is available through The Florida Channel.Why the Florida Supreme Court rejected retroactive applicationChief Justice Couriel authored the majority opinion. The court examined whether the Florida Legislature had clearly stated that section 627.70152 should apply to policies issued before July 1, 2021. Under the court’s established two-step test, it first looks for a clear legislative intention to make a law retroactive. Only if that intention is established does it consider whether retroactive application would violate constitutional principles. The court found no clear command in the statute. It considered the phrase “all suits” in section 627.70152(1), which describes the lawsuits covered by the provision, but concluded that the wording did not establish that the law extended to suits involving policies issued before its effective date.The court also rejected the Fourth District’s reasoning that the Legislature would have expressly excluded older policies if it intended the law to apply only to newer ones. According to the Supreme Court, the absence of language limiting a statute to future policies does not amount to clear evidence that lawmakers intended it to apply retroactively. The statute’s stated effective date also weighed against applying it to earlier policies. Universal argued that the notice requirement was procedural rather than substantive. The court disagreed after considering the law as a whole. The provision did more than establish a filing procedure: it delayed an insured’s ability to sue and gave insurers an additional opportunity to evaluate and pay claims before litigation. It also prescribed dismissal for noncompliance and, under subsection (8)(b), restricted recovery of attorney fees incurred before dismissal. That fee provision was subsequently repealed in 2022. The court concluded that these effects altered the rights and obligations of policyholders and insurers under property insurance contracts. It therefore declined to apply the notice requirement to Hughes’s 2019 policy.What the ruling means for Florida property insurance policyholdersThe key date is when the policy was issued, rather than simply when the damage occurred or when a lawsuit was filed. The Supreme Court held that section 627.70152’s presuit-notice requirement does not apply retroactively to policies issued before the provision took effect on July 1, 2021. Because Hughes’s policy was issued in April 2019, her lawsuit could not be dismissed for failing to comply with that later requirement. The ruling does not eliminate the pre-suit notice requirement for all property insurance lawsuits. The requirement remains applicable to policies issued on or after July 1, 2021, subject to the statute’s terms and exceptions. The decision addresses policies issued before that date and does not resolve the underlying dispute over whether Universal paid Hughes the correct amount for her water damage.Justice Tanenbaum wrote separately, concurring with the outcome but offering a different legal rationale. He pointed to section 624.21 of the Florida Statutes, which provides that amendments to the Insurance Code operate prospectively unless a contrary legislative intention is specified. In his view, that provision independently supported applying the notice requirement only prospectively because the Legislature had not expressly directed retroactive application.The Supreme Court approved the Sixth District’s decision in Hughes to the extent it was consistent with the opinion and disapproved the Fourth District’s contrary decision in Cole. That resolved the conflict among Florida’s district appeals courts over the reach of the 2021 notice requirement. The opinion states that it is not final until the period for filing a motion for rehearing expires and any timely motion is decided. The ruling does not determine whether Hughes is ultimately entitled to a larger insurance payment; it establishes that the 2021 pre-suit notice requirement cannot be used retroactively to dismiss her lawsuit over a policy issued in 2019.You use AI every day. articles.title: A Pennsylvania couple spent nearly six years fighting to add a drive-through to their 5-7-acre truck stop after officials refused permission, but an October 27 appeals ruling overturned the denial and revived their plan
articles.summary: A drive-through window may seem like a small addition to an established convenience store, but for one Pennsylvania couple, getting permission to build
articles.body: A drive-through window may seem like a small addition to an established convenience store, but for one Pennsylvania couple, getting permission to build one turned into a legal battle lasting nearly six years. Their proposal involved a 5-7-acre truck stop that already sold freshly prepared food and served motorists around the clock. However, local zoning officials refused permission, arguing that township regulations prohibited drive-through facilities at convenience stores.The dispute reached the Pennsylvania Commonwealth Court, which ruled on October 27, 2026, in Jyotsna Jivani and Anil Jivani v. East Lampeter Township Zoning Hearing Board and East Lampeter Township, according to the court opinion available on Justia. The court overturned the lower court's decision upholding the denial, finding conflicting provisions in the township's zoning ordinance. It also recognised the proposed facility as a natural expansion of the existing business and sent the case back to the zoning board for further proceedings.A truck stop looking to expand its food serviceJyotsna and Anil Jivani own a property at 2622 Lincoln Highway East in East Lampeter Township, Lancaster County. The approximately 5-7-acre site contains a convenience store, petrol station and truck stop operating as a lawful nonconforming use in an agricultural zoning district. The store operates 24 hours a day and includes food counters operated by Subway and Champ's Fried Chicken. Customers can purchase freshly prepared meals, while passenger vehicles and tractor-trailers use separate fuelling facilities.The couple wanted to add a drive-through window so customers could order and collect food without entering the store. The proposal was influenced partly by changing customer preferences during the COVID-19 pandemic, when some customers, particularly elderly people, were uncomfortable entering indoor spaces. During a December 2020 zoning board hearing, Anil Jivani explained that the franchise was insisting on curbside delivery or a pickup window. He argued that the facility would give existing customers another way to purchase food rather than introduce an entirely new business.Why township officials rejected the proposalThe couple submitted their zoning permit application around October 2020. After the township denied it, they appealed to the East Lampeter Township Zoning Hearing Board in November 2020, seeking approval or, alternatively, a special exception or variance. Their proposal involved replacing an existing bus-passenger drop-off lane beside the store with drive-through lanes. The design included a nine-foot-wide lane that would divide into two lanes, allowing vehicles to bypass the queue when necessary.The facility would provide approximately 120 feet of queuing space, accommodating four cars before the ordering kiosk and four afterwards. Only passenger vehicles would be allowed to use it. The construction also required a 38-square-foot addition at the rear of the building, offset by removing an equivalent area near the front entrance. Consequently, there would be no net increase in the store's usable floor area.Township officials argued that the zoning ordinance prohibited drive-through facilities at convenience stores. The board accepted this interpretation and denied the application on January 14, 2021. The Lancaster County Court of Common Pleas upheld the decision on August 14, 2025.Appeals court identifies conflicting zoning rulesThe Pennsylvania Commonwealth Court examined two provisions of the township's zoning ordinance. Section 2020 defined a convenience store as a retail establishment selling groceries and ready-to-eat food, but excluded businesses with drive-through facilities. However, Section 23200 contained specific provisions addressing drive-through service lanes at convenience stores, including requirements for vehicle queuing.The judges found that the two provisions contradicted each other. Under Section 603.1 of Pennsylvania's Municipalities Planning Code, ambiguities in zoning restrictions must be interpreted in favour of the property owner. The township's zoning officer had testified that the permissive language was left in the ordinance by mistake during a 2016 overhaul. However, the court found that the conflicting provisions created ambiguity and that state law required the matter to be resolved in favour of the property owners. It therefore concluded that the zoning rules did permit drive-through facilities at convenience stores.Judges recognise the proposal as a natural expansionThe court also considered whether the proposed drive-through represented a natural expansion of the couple's existing nonconforming business. It found that the facility would not fundamentally change the store's primary activity of selling retail goods and prepared food. Instead, it would provide another way for customers to access products already available inside.The judges considered the property's history, including a 1988 zoning decision recognising a fast-food restaurant as part of the approved use, with seating for 30 to 35 customers. They also noted that the proposed changes involved limited physical alterations, no increase in overall floor area or paved lot coverage, and the replacement of a largely unused bus drop-off area.On October 27, 2026, the Commonwealth Court reversed the lower court's order and remanded the case to the East Lampeter Township Zoning Hearing Board for further proceedings consistent with its opinion. The ruling is non-precedential and does not automatically grant final construction approval. However, it removes the legal basis for the original denial and gives the couple another opportunity to pursue their proposed drive-through after years of litigation.You use AI every day. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Saturday invited people to join a march in the national capital on Sunday before reaching Ramlila Maidan, where the INDIA bloc is scheduled to hold a mega rally on November 1.However, Delhi Police sources told news agency ANI that no permission had been sought for the proposed march from Connaught Place.In a post on X, Rahul shared the route and schedule of the march, saying, "See you tomorrow, let's walk together."According to his post, the march will begin at the Minto Road junction near Connaught Place at noon on Sunday. Participants will proceed towards Ajmeri Gate before concluding at Ramlila Maidan.Responding to Rahul's announcement, Delhi Police sources told ANI that no application had been received seeking permission for a march from Connaught Place. They added that MPs and political leaders were free to travel in their private vehicles to the Constitution Club, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence or any other location of their choice.The sources also pointed out that Jantar Mantar, traditionally a designated venue for protests in the capital, has been de-notified as a protest site. They said Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), which restricts assemblies and gatherings, is currently in force across the New Delhi area, including the vicinity of the Election Commission.Police said elaborate security arrangements would be made at Ramlila Maidan for Sunday's rally. Personnel from multiple Delhi Police districts, including the Central District, will be deployed along with paramilitary forces.Meanwhile, INDIA bloc leaders are scheduled to hold a public programme on the proposed impeachment of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar on Saturday at 3.30 pm at 10, Rajaji Marg, the residence of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge.The programme was postponed from Friday due to rain in the national capital. Announcing the decision, Gandhi said the leaders had agreed to reschedule it to avoid inconvenience to senior members.Speaking to reporters in Delhi on Friday, Rahul said, "By consensus, we have decided to postpone today's program (public impeachment programme against CEC) to tomorrow at the same time because of rain. We felt that it would be uncomfortable for seniors to sit in the rain, and we will hold the same program tomorrow."He also urged political parties, civil society members, journalists and other citizens to join the INDIA bloc's November 1 march to Ramlila Maidan."The day after, we have a march to Ramlila Maidan. All the opposition, everybody who wants to come: political, non-political, social, service people, civil society people, journalists. Both the programs are about the demolition of Indian democracy by Narendra Modi, by Amit Shah, by Gyanesh Kumar and his crew in the Election Commission," he said.Raebareli MP further alleged that Union home minister Amit Shah was trying to prevent people from travelling to Delhi to attend the rally."The home minister is trying his best to stop people from coming into Delhi, trying to ensure that our party members, common people who want to come from UP, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Haryana, Telangana, Punjab, are being stopped. And they're trying their best," former Congress chief said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Psychology says people who treat their purchases as part of a collection may find the shopping process more enjoyable, as research involving 3,306 participants reveals how a collecting mindset changes what we want
articles.summary: People have a dream of a closet that doesn’t just consist of clothes, rather a space that holds stories, culture and respect for tradition.
articles.body: People have a dream of a closet that doesn’t just consist of clothes, rather a space that holds stories, culture and respect for tradition. For instance, one can wish to own a collection of sarees that are acquired from different corners of India engrained with hard work of local artisans. They wouldn’t simply be a collection of clothes rather an exhibition of the rich textile and handcraft culture of India. It seems obvious that such people enjoy shopping more than those who shop without any such consideration. Well, psychology has now proven this popular assumption with an elaborate study proving how collecting mindset changes what we want.There is a certain joy in finding that one incomplete piece from a collection, it could be a figurine, a collectible or the last book of a favourite series. The excitement builds over time, with waiting, anticipation, search efforts and then finally finding it at a small store somewhere. People may even save meticulously to complete their collections, thus, making them happier than just getting something they need. Let us dive into what psychology says about such people and their relative joy while shopping.A study titled ‘The Collecting Mindset: Viewing Purchasing as Collecting Enhances Acquisition Experience and Product Desirability’ examines how thinking of a purchase as an addition to a collection can change the shopping experience. The study involved 3,306 participants and found that adopting a collecting mindset could make the process of acquiring something more enjoyable. It can even increase the product's desirability. In other words, sometimes the thrill is not just about what we are buying. It is about what that purchase means in the larger scheme of things.The psychology of finding the missing pieceImpulsive shopping often makes you feel guilty later. The lack of thought behind the purchase- do you need it, do you like it or do you even have enough money—makes you question if the purchase was even necessary. But spending on something you have thought about, or rather dreamt about for a long time will only bring you happiness.The researchers found that when people were encouraged to view products as additions to their collections rather than as isolated purchases, their attention shifted towards the experience of building the collection. Searching for the right item became part of the pleasure, rather than merely a task to complete before reaching the checkout. This enjoyment, in turn, could make the product itself seem more desirable.It is a subtle distinction, but one that helps explain why collectors can spend hours browsing, comparing and hunting for something specific. The search is not simply an obstacle between them and the object. It is part of the reward.From ordinary shopping to a personal treasure huntSome people collect fridge magnets from every city they visit. Others have a soft spot for illustrated editions of classic novels, quirky earrings, vinyl records or tiny ceramic animals. Even a collection of postcards can become a record of places visited and memories made. What matters is the sense of connection between the objects. Each new addition has a place in a story that is already unfolding.The research also highlights an important condition: the new item should meaningfully advance the collection, and the collection should connect with an identity the person values. If the purchase feels irrelevant to that identity, the positive effect may weaken or even reverse. The researchers also point to active involvement in the search as an important part of creating an enjoyable acquisition experience.Why retailers love a collecting mindsetThere is another side to this discovery, and it has plenty to do with how brands sell products.Ever noticed how certain products are released in themed series, seasonal editions or matching sets? Think of collectible toys, limited-edition packaging, beauty products in coordinated shades or travel souvenirs designed to encourage you to bring home one from every destination.These strategies give shoppers a reason to return. Rather than asking whether they want one product, the question becomes whether they want to complete the set or discover the next addition.The above research offers a psychological explanation for why this approach is adopted by brands. Brands utilise this technique by encouraging consumers to see an item as part of a meaningful collection. They can also make the search itself more engaging and the product more appealing.However, this collective mindset can also have consequences for your wallet. A separate 2024 study titled ‘Collective influence: How the collection mindset shapes consumer spending and price perceptions’ has studied these consequences. It studies that thinking in terms of collections could influence how consumers evaluate prices and make subsequent purchases. The researchers found that a collecting mindset could make people less sensitive to price changes, partly because they evaluated items more for enjoyment than for practical usefulness.Thus, give your next purchase a thought as it is not just about having a collection of material things, but creating an assortment of emotions.You use AI every day. articles.body: NALASOPARA: Eight people were seriously injured after a lift in a seven-storey residential building, Dhananjay Avenue, at Patankar Park in Nalasopara (West), came crashing down on Saturday around noon.The injured were rushed to a nearby hospital by fellow residents.Nalasopara police visited the spot and inspected the site after being alerted about the incident.According to residents, the eight people were travelling in the lift from the fifth floor to the ground floor around 12 pm when it suddenly plunged down at high speed.Hearing a loud impact, other residents rushed to the spot and managed to break open the lift door after considerable effort.They rescued the injured occupants and shifted them to a nearby hospital, where they are currently undergoing treatment.The injured include advocate Satish Bhondve, a resident of the building, and seven of his guests."The occupants fell on top of one another inside the lift. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Amid ongoing resentment within the National Conference camp over the recent cabinet expansion, Jammu and Kashmir minister Javed Rana on
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Amid ongoing resentment within the National Conference camp over the recent cabinet expansion, Jammu and Kashmir minister Javed Rana on Saturday said the party remained strong, with no resentment among its ranks, and dismissed speculation that Srinagar MP Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi's planned exit would affect the party."If Agha Sahab decides to part ways, he will do so alone. If he leaves, he leaves by himself... Why would it affect the party?" Rana said, responding to questions about Ruhullah's decision to resign from the party and his Lok Sabha seat on November 3.Rana said the government was robust under chief minister Omar Abdullah and the party organisation, under the leadership of Farooq Abdullah, stood firm."There is no resentment (in JKNC). The Jammu & Kashmir National Conference is strong, the government under the leadership of the chief minister is robust, and the organisation, under the leadership of Dr Farooq Sahab, stands firm, as solid as a rock," he said.Rana also said the reported discontent within the party was due to the limited number of ministerial positions, adding that several legislators aspired to join the cabinet but the available slots were restricted.He also expressed hope that statehood would be restored soon and more ministers would be appointed."There are celebrations taking place across J&K regarding the cabinet expansion. I do not see any signs of discontent anywhere. Was any statement issued on their behalf? I do not believe there is any substantive evidence to support such claims," he said."There is no real resentment; it is simply a case of 'every MLA wishing to become a minister', but the available slots are very limited. Insha'Allah, statehood will be restored soon, and insha'Allah, ministers will be appointed," he added.Cracks widened in the National Conference following the J&K cabinet expansion and a meeting of party legislators. The developments have also coincided with Ruhullah's announcement that he would quit the party and resign from his parliamentary seat on November 3.Meanwhile, according to sources, over a dozen party legislators met on Friday evening at the residence of Qaiser Jamshaid Lone, who represents the Lolab constituency, with several others joining the meeting online.They decided to seek the resignation of the entire council of ministers and demand that a new cabinet be formed through consensus, based on merit and in keeping with democratic principles, sources said. They also decided to seek the resignation of chief minister's advisor Nasir Ahmad Wani.JKNC Kashmir president Showkat Ahmad Mir acknowledged that some party members had expressed concerns following the cabinet expansion, describing such differences as part of the party's internal democratic process."Following the expansion of the cabinet, some individuals expressed their concerns, which they are entitled to do as part of the internal democracy of the party. Regarding the meeting that took place yesterday, some MLAs with whom I am in touch mentioned receiving a phone call about a 'Darbar Move', where they discussed various pros and cons. Once they left, the situation was blown out of proportion with claims of 27 members involved, largely fuelled by the BJP, which is keen on spreading such rumours," Mir told news agency ANI."The BJP promised the people of Jammu that they would restore statehood and secured votes on that basis; today, the people of Jammu are rebuking them severely," he added.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.summary: Hundreds of residents have been evacuated from the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky following a humanitarian ceasefire brokered by US First Lady
articles.body: Hundreds of residents have been evacuated from the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky following a humanitarian ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump, with three planes carrying evacuees landing at an airport in Belarus on Saturday, according to media reports.The residents, who wished to return to Ukraine, were taken by bus through the Crimean peninsula to the Russian town of Anapa before being flown to Gomel in Belarus. They will travel onwards to Ukraine through a border crossing, Belarusian state news agency Belta reported, according to Reuters.The evacuation took place on Friday as part of a joint relief operation involving the opposing sides, marking the first operation of its kind in four years and eight months of the war. Residents were reportedly starving and exhausted.According to the BBC, Russian and Ukrainian authorities confirmed that hundreds of people had been evacuated from the devastated town. The operation was carried out during a temporary ceasefire that allowed the road out of Oleshky to be cleared of landmines.A ceasefire covering the entire frontline region of Kherson had been in force since Tuesday. The BBC described it as the longest and most extensive ceasefire since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.Residents wishing to leave were given a four-hour window on Friday. A convoy of 25 buses was deployed to transport up to 750 people from the town by 2 pm local time. Ambulances were also arranged for people with limited mobility. BBC reported.Russia's human rights ombudsman Yana Lantratova said the evacuation had taken place without incident."Everything unfolded without any incidents, and both sides noted the high level of organisation," she said.Ukrainian authorities confirmed that the evacuees were travelling towards southern Russia before continuing to Ukraine through Belarus.Melania Trump said that "all elements of the convoy, including the safe passageway in and out of Oleshky, was established through mutual agreement between Russian and Ukrainian leaders".Lantratova and her Ukrainian counterpart also made a joint appeal to the US first lady for similar humanitarian operations to be organised regularly.Speaking on Friday evening, Lantratova said they had requested that "humanitarian missions such as this one, delivering aid to residents in need, be conducted on a regular basis under the coordination of Mrs Melania Trump".You use AI every day. articles.title: Bosnian electrician Petar Tubic rescued a two-kilogram bear cub in 2019; six years later, the 150-kilogram bear still tries to climb onto his lap, while his home has become a refuge for rescued animals
articles.summary: In the mountains of Bosnia and Herzegovina, an unexpected rescue has grown into a remarkable bond between a man and a bear.
articles.body: In the mountains of Bosnia and Herzegovina, an unexpected rescue has grown into a remarkable bond between a man and a bear. Petar Tubic, an electrician living on Mount Ozren, took in an abandoned bear cub in 2019 and raised her after finding her alone in the forest. Six years later, the bear, named Masa, weighs around 150 kilograms but continues to seek the closeness she enjoyed as a cub. An Associated Press report published on October 24, 2026, documented their unusual friendship, which has also transformed Tubic’s property into a haven for rescued wildlife. Coverage by Reuters Connect has similarly drawn attention to his growing family of animals.From a vulnerable cub to a 150-kilogram bearWhen Tubic found Masa in 2019, she weighed just two kilograms. Separated from her mother and left alone in the forest, the young bear was unlikely to survive without help. Tubic took her home, where he fed her milk and fruit and helped her regain her strength. What began as an act of compassion soon changed his everyday life. Caring for a bear was unfamiliar territory for the electrician, who had to learn how to meet the animal’s needs as she grew.Today, Masa is a powerful adult bear, yet some of her behaviour appears to reflect the bond formed during her earliest months. She still approaches Tubic affectionately and sometimes attempts to climb onto his lap, despite weighing roughly 150 kilograms. Their interactions can be playful, but her size makes them potentially dangerous. Even an affectionate movement from a bear can cause serious injury, and Tubic has experienced bruises and torn clothing during their encounters.A friendship that changed an entire householdMasa is not the only bear living on Tubic’s property. He has also taken in another female bear, Ljubica, expanding the responsibilities that came with his first rescue. Over time, the property on Mount Ozren has developed into a refuge for animals that need care. Alongside the two bears, Tubic looks after wolves, deer, raccoons and numerous other animals.The growing collection has attracted visitors who want to see the animals and learn about the unusual relationship between Tubic and his bears. What was once a private act of rescue has consequently become a local attraction, bringing wider attention to his work. Tubic lives with his wife, Milica, and their nine-year-old daughter, Eva. Although he works as an electrician, his interests also include hiking, caving and paragliding. Animals, however, have become a central part of family life.Why the bears may never return to the wildDespite the affection between Tubic and the bears, their future presents a difficult question. He has considered releasing them into their natural habitat but worries that years of close contact with humans have made them too accustomed to people to live safely in the wild. For now, Masa and Ljubica remain on the family property, where Tubic continues to care for them. Their story has also drawn attention to the challenges of looking after wild animals rescued at a young age, particularly when they grow into powerful adults.A separate report by Anadolu Agency, published before the Associated Press account, documented how the refuge developed from a former paragliding base into a sanctuary for orphaned bears and other animals. The facility, known as Naša Maša, has become a destination for visitors interested in wildlife and animal care. The bond between Tubic and Masa may look like a story of an unusually affectionate animal, but it also reflects the lasting responsibilities that follow a rescue. A cub that once depended on milk and shelter has grown into a large wild animal whose needs require continued attention.For Tubic, the experience has brought him closer to a world he had not previously understood. His life changed when he took in a helpless cub, and the refuge that followed has given numerous animals a place to live. The relationship is extraordinary, but it is not without its risks. Bears remain powerful wild animals, even when raised around people, and their strength makes careful management essential. On Mount Ozren, the challenge is to sustain the bond while ensuring that the animals receive the care and protection they need.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A 117-year-old North Carolina basilica battled leaks and storm damage, then underwent a $7.7 million first phase of restoration; it reopened daily to visitors, while the full preservation effort could top $30 million
articles.summary: A century-old architectural landmark in Asheville, North Carolina, has reached a major milestone after years of deterioration threatened its distinctive
articles.body: A century-old architectural landmark in Asheville, North Carolina, has reached a major milestone after years of deterioration threatened its distinctive dome and historic masonry. The Basilica of Saint Lawrence completed the first phase of a $7.7 million restoration and marked its reopening with a ceremony on October 10, 2026. According to Catholic News Herald, local outlet HERE Asheville and public radio station BPR News, the project focused on stopping water leaks, repairing storm damage and protecting the building for future generations. The restoration is part of a much larger preservation effort that could eventually cost more than $30 million. While the latest work has addressed some of the building’s most urgent problems, further repairs will depend on funding and the progress of subsequent phases.A historic landmark threatened by water damageLocated in downtown Asheville, the Basilica of Saint Lawrence is known for its distinctive elliptical dome and intricate tile construction. Designed under the supervision of Spanish architect Rafael Guastavino Sr., the church was completed in 1909 and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.Over the years, leaks and deteriorating building materials made extensive repairs increasingly urgent. Hurricane Helene, which struck western North Carolina in September 2024, added to the damage and reinforced the need to protect the structure.The restoration began in October 2025 after years of planning, assessments and fundraising. Preservation specialists and construction teams were tasked with addressing water intrusion while safeguarding the architectural features that make the basilica distinctive. The first phase was budgeted at approximately $7.7 million, with contributions from parishioners, donors and grants helping fund the work.What the $7.7 million restoration includedThe initial phase concentrated on the building’s exterior and structural protection, particularly areas vulnerable to water damage. Work included replacing the copper covering on the iconic dome, installing new storm drains and gutters, repairing cornices and restoring the dome’s oculus skylight. Crews also stabilised masonry above the Marian Chapel and addressed damage associated with Hurricane Helene.These repairs were intended to prevent further water from entering the building and to stabilise vulnerable sections of the historic structure. Stopping the leaks was particularly important because continued moisture exposure could threaten masonry, interior finishes and other architectural details.The project involved specialist preservation work rather than routine maintenance. Guastavino’s distinctive tile-and-mortar construction requires care to retain the building’s historic character while improving its long-term durability. The completion of the first phase therefore represents an important step, rather than the end of the basilica’s preservation needs.An architectural legacy worth preservingGuastavino’s work is known for its distinctive tile vaulting, a construction technique that uses layers of thin tiles and mortar to create strong, elegant structures. His work can be seen in prominent American landmarks, including Grand Central Terminal and Ellis Island in New York.The Asheville basilica is particularly significant because it represents one of his most ambitious architectural projects. Construction began in the early 1900s, but Guastavino died in 1908, before the church was completed. His son, Rafael Guastavino Jr., helped bring the project to completion in 1909.Preservation efforts have been under consideration for years, with assessments and fundraising campaigns laying the groundwork for the current project. The Basilica Preservation Fund, a nonprofit organisation established in 2008, has helped raise money to protect the building and its architectural features.Reopening marks a milestone, not the finish lineThe October 10 ceremony brought together Bishop Michael Martin, parishioners, donors and preservation specialists to mark the completion of the first phase. The reopening was a significant moment for a church that continued to hold Masses and sacraments during construction, even as weekday visitor access was restricted.However, the restoration remains a multi-stage undertaking, with the overall cost potentially exceeding $30 million. Future work will depend on continued fundraising and the condition of the building as further repairs are planned.There is also an important distinction between the ceremonial reopening and unrestricted daily access. The basilica’s official website, updated October 22, lists limited visiting hours during the ongoing restoration and announces a revised schedule beginning November 2. Visitors should check the official website⁠ before planning a visit.For Asheville, the completed work is more than a construction milestone. It is an investment in a historic structure that has shaped the city’s skyline for more than a century. By addressing the most urgent threats first, the restoration team has taken a crucial step towards ensuring that the basilica’s architectural and cultural legacy can endure for generations to come.You use AI every day. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Saturday said that the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls was initiated to remove anti-BJP votes as he kickstarted the INDIA bloc's public impeachment motion against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of voter irregularities.Moving the impeachment motion in the mock Parliament, Kharge said Gyanesh Kumar was running the Election Commission under the direct instructions of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah.Here are the top quotes from his speech:CEC Gyanesh Kumar is running the Commission under the direct instructions of the Prime Minister and the Home Minister. Seven months ago, 193 opposition MPs moved a motion in both Houses of Parliament to remove the CEC.However, our notices were rejected, and no cognisance was taken of them. Therefore, the motion we have brought forward today is aimed at safeguarding the dignity of a constitutional institution. We hold no personal grudge against the CEC.Our intention is for the Election Commission to function impartially, in line with the spirit of the Constitution, so that the common man's trust in it remains intact. We must ensure that the voting rights of vulnerable sections, women, and the youth are not surreptitiously deleted from a computer by someone sitting in Delhi.Since 2014, every possible conspiracy has been hatched to seize and retain power. They have stolen MPs, broken up political parties, toppled governments, and used electoral bonds, the ED, and the CBI, and now they are stealing votes.We have hundreds of examples of such vote theft. Gyanesh Kumar is able to facilitate this theft due to the 2023 Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act.This bill was passed in December 2023 after suspending 145 opposition MPs. It is shameful and a disgrace. articles.title: Minecraft creator Markus Persson paid $70 million for a 22,300 sq ft Beverly Hills mansion in 2014; 12 years later he has listed it for exactly the same price, complete with a private nightclub and a $200,000 candy room
articles.summary: Markus Persson, the Swedish billionaire behind the global gaming phenomenon Minecraft, has listed his extravagant Beverly Hills mansion for $70 million,
articles.body: Markus Persson, the Swedish billionaire behind the global gaming phenomenon Minecraft, has listed his extravagant Beverly Hills mansion for $70 million, asking exactly what he paid for the property in December 2014. The 22,300-square-foot estate features eight bedrooms, 15 bathrooms, a private nightclub and a candy room that reportedly cost $200,000. According to the Los Angeles Times and The Wall Street Journal, the listing comes as Los Angeles’ luxury housing market faces a different climate from the boom years when Persson first purchased the property. The mansion, perched on approximately an acre overlooking Los Angeles, was built by property developer Bruce Makowsky, known for creating lavish homes packed with unusual amenities. Persson acquired it shortly after selling his gaming company, Mojang, to Microsoft for $2.5 billion.Inside the mansion with a private nightclubThe estate is designed as much for entertainment as for everyday living. Alongside its eight bedrooms and 15 bathrooms, the property includes a recording studio, a private nightclub with a DJ booth and bar, a movie theatre, a swimming pool and an elevator. A 2,500-bottle wine cellar is another highlight, while the home’s distinctive candy room was among the features that attracted attention when the property first went on the market.Earlier reporting by Forbes and the Los Angeles Times described additional extravagant details, including an automated, curved glass door opening towards an infinity pool, a large onyx dining table and a garage designed to showcase luxury cars. The house was originally offered fully furnished, with designer furniture and other high-end fittings included in the sale. Persson bought the property after reportedly outbidding celebrity couple Jay-Z and Beyoncé, who had toured the house several times. The couple later purchased a Bel-Air mansion of their own.Why the $70 million asking price stands outThe asking price is particularly striking because it matches the amount Persson paid 12 years ago. Although the median home value in Los Angeles has more than doubled over that period, the ultra-luxury market operates differently from the broader housing market.In 2014, the mansion had been listed for $85 million before Persson acquired it for $70 million. Its current listing price therefore represents no nominal increase over his original purchase price, although the eventual sale proceeds, carrying costs and any changes to the property’s condition will determine the financial outcome.The asking price also reflects the challenges facing sellers of trophy properties. Elaborate amenities and architectural features can make a home distinctive, but they do not guarantee that a buyer will pay the seller’s preferred amount. The experience of Makowsky, the home’s original developer, illustrates that distinction. His other high-profile luxury properties have attracted ambitious asking prices but have sometimes sold for considerably less after extended marketing.The fortune behind the Minecraft creator’s mansionPersson, widely known by his gaming-community nickname Notch, founded Mojang Studios in 2009. The company released Minecraft in 2011, and the sandbox game subsequently became the best-selling video game of all time. Microsoft acquired Mojang in 2014 for $2.5 billion, providing Persson with the fortune that helped finance his Beverly Hills purchase. The deal transformed the independent game developer into one of the technology industry’s best-known billionaire creators.The mansion’s current listing comes with no guarantee that it will sell for the asking price. If a buyer agrees to the full $70 million, the property could become Beverly Hills’ most expensive home sale of 2026, according to the Los Angeles Times. The final price, however, will depend on negotiations and market demand. For now, the listing puts one of Beverly Hills’ most recognisable celebrity-owned properties back in the spotlight, with its nightclub, candy room and elaborate entertainment spaces offering a glimpse into the extravagant side of luxury real estate.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: In 1982, a couple came from Lebanon to Australia and later raised four children in a Melbourne home; when it sold for A$960,000 in October 2026, the buyers' promise not to demolish it moved them to tears
articles.summary: A Melbourne couple who spent more than four decades building a family life in their home experienced an emotional farewell when the property was sold at
articles.body: A Melbourne couple who spent more than four decades building a family life in their home experienced an emotional farewell when the property was sold at auction for A$960,000. The four-bedroom house in Maidstone, in Melbourne's west, had been their family home since they arrived in Australia from Lebanon in 1982. Although the sale marked the end of their time there, the buyers' decision to retain the existing house rather than demolish it brought them to tears. According to a report published by realestate.com.au on October 30, 2026, the winning buyers made the promise after the auction, giving the longtime owners reassurance that the home would continue to stand.A Melbourne home that held four decades of family memoriesThe property at 26 Marsh Street, Maidstone, became an important part of the couple's life after they settled in Australia. Nelson Alexander auctioneer Ryan Currie told realestate.com.au that the couple had arrived from Lebanon in 1982 and subsequently raised four children in the house. More than 40 years of family life had taken place within its walls, making the property much more than a residential asset for its owners.Two of the couple's four children attended the auction as their parents prepared to leave the home. After spending decades there, the sellers were planning to downsize to a low-maintenance property in Taylors Lakes. The move would bring a change in their living arrangements, but the emotional connection to the Maidstone house remained strong. The property sits on a 586-square-metre block and attracted attention during the sales campaign because of its north-facing orientation and potential for redevelopment. According to Currie, several developers inspected the site, although none attended the auction.The A$960,000 auction and the buyers' decisionThe four-bedroom house was sold on Saturday, October 24, 2026, for A$960,000. The final price was A$50,000 above its published reserve of A$910,000. The auction attracted interest from buyers with different plans for the property. A local family hoping to demolish the existing house and rebuild finished as the underbidder. However, the successful purchasers had a different intention. They wanted to live in the existing home and planned to retain it rather than knock it down.That decision became particularly meaningful to the former owners. After the auction, the couple were eager to meet the winning buyers. When the purchasers told them they intended to keep the house, the conversation prompted an emotional response. Currie recalled that both the husband and wife burst into tears after hearing the news. Their reaction reflected the importance of knowing that the home where they had raised their children would not immediately be demolished following the sale.Why the promise mattered to the sellersFor homeowners, selling a property can involve more than agreeing on a price. A house that has been occupied for decades can hold memories of family milestones, everyday routines and the experience of raising children. In this case, the couple had lived in the Maidstone property for more than four decades, making the prospect of its demolition especially difficult. The buyers' intention to preserve the existing house offered a degree of reassurance during an otherwise significant transition. While the couple would no longer live there, the building itself would remain part of the neighbourhood and continue to serve as a family home.The sale also demonstrated how buyers can approach the same property with different priorities. The underbidding family saw an opportunity to demolish and rebuild, while the successful purchasers preferred to retain the existing residence. The property's redevelopment potential had attracted interest from developers during the campaign, but the eventual outcome was shaped by buyers who wanted to occupy the house as it stood.A new chapter for the Maidstone propertyCurrie said moments like the sellers' emotional reaction made his work rewarding, particularly after a challenging period for Melbourne's property market. The auction was not simply the completion of a transaction for the couple. It marked the end of a long chapter that began when they arrived in Australia and established their family home.The former owners are now preparing for a smaller, low-maintenance home in Taylors Lakes, while the successful buyers intend to make the Maidstone house their family residence. The A$960,000 sale therefore brought a change of ownership without the immediate demolition the sellers had feared. For a couple who raised four children in the house after moving from Lebanon in 1982, the buyers' promise offered an emotional parting gift. Their family may be moving on, but the home that witnessed more than 40 years of their lives is set to remain standing.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A Los Angeles man lost his office job in 2020 and began selling plants from a 600-sq-ft apartment; six years later, his family business has sold over 100,000 plants in 2026 and now brings in millions in annual sales
articles.summary: Brandon Hurst never planned to become a plant seller.
articles.body: Brandon Hurst never planned to become a plant seller. In 2020, he was working as an administrative assistant at a Los Angeles real estate office and living paycheck to paycheck when he lost his job during the Covid-19 pandemic. Looking for a way to make extra money, he began reselling items on Facebook Marketplace, then noticed a woman selling inexpensive plants bought from a dollar store. He decided to try the same idea, posting his first listing, a pink plant in a pink pot, in April or May 2020. According to PEOPLE, customers began messaging him almost immediately, and that small experiment became the foundation of a multimillion-dollar family business.Six years later, Hurst’s company has sold more than 100,000 plants in 2026 alone and now generates millions of dollars in gross annual sales, as per the report. What once operated from his roughly 600-square-foot apartment now employs 24 people, sells about 5,000 plants each week, and processes around 1,000 orders a day. The business has also moved into a 3,000-square-foot greenhouse in Los Angeles’ San Fernando Valley, giving Hurst and his family room to grow beyond the apartment where it all began. Read more about Hurst's simple business idea, as reported by PEOPLE and ET, here:A side hustle that became a family businessHurst’s first plant sale was not backed by experience, formal training, or a detailed business plan. He had never owned a plant before, let alone considered himself a plant person. But the response to his first Facebook Marketplace listing was strong enough to convince him to keep going. Within six months, he, his husband Josh, and his mother were working on the business full time, selling hundreds of plants each week from his balcony.At first, his mother encouraged him to keep a traditional job rather than take a risk on plants. As sales grew, however, she became one of his biggest supporters, driving him to a local flower market to purchase wholesale plants. Josh helped manage the operation from their apartment, while Hurst discovered that working with plants gave him something more valuable than income. He told People that arranging succulents and designing a window box for one of his first customers made him feel peaceful, a feeling that eventually convinced him the business could become a career.The early days were physically demanding. Shelving units filled the balcony, dining room, and living room, while Hurst’s former bedroom became a livestreaming space. At one point, the family was selling more than 1,000 plants a week from the apartment, sometimes reaching 2,000. Hurst recalled that they were “shoving plants in places” they never expected, turning every available corner of the home into storage, packing space, or a sales area.When TikTok turned attention into salesIn 2021, a customer who worked as a social media manager suggested that Hurst claim the name “Brandon The Plant Guy” across social platforms. He began posting short TikTok videos with plant care advice, including guidance on caring for snake plants and choosing easy varieties for beginners. Some videos passed one million views, and he built an audience of 100,000 followers before TikTok Shop officially launched in 2023. His following has since grown to more than 268,000. Interestingly, he has also named his professional LinkedIn profile so.Hurst received an early invitation to sell through TikTok Shop and hosted his first livestream on April 18, 2023. He expected to sell about 30 plants. Instead, he sold 250 in roughly three hours, far beyond what he and his family had prepared for. New sellers were limited to 300 orders during a probationary period, and the business repeatedly reached that cap. With no employees at the time, Hurst, Josh, and his mother packed orders late into the night, filling the living room with nursery bags and plants.Neighbours and customers eventually came to the apartment to help. Hurst described the experience as trying to build a plane while it was already flying. The livestream format was particularly successful because it allowed him to show his personality and answer questions as they came in, and build trust with shoppers still hesitant about buying plants on a new platform.Auctions changed the way business was doneBy the beginning of 2026, Hurst had dramatically changed his sales model. Rather than listing plants at set prices of about $16 or $35, he started making each sale an auction during his livestreams. People says profits have tripled since the switch. The auctions turned ordinary plant purchases into an interactive experience, with viewers bidding, joking, and competing for plants while Hurst narrated the sales in a playful, conversational style.The approach has helped the company scale while keeping the personal connection that made it successful. Hurst hosts live sales several nights a week, sometimes for six to eight hours at a time. Rather than presenting the livestreams as hard selling, he treats them as community gatherings where customers can ask questions, share stories, and feel part of something.Some customers have shown remarkable loyalty. Hurst recalled one longtime customer bidding $200 for a basic pothos in a six-inch pot, even though he knew the plant was not worth that amount on the market. The golden pothos has become one of his best sellers, with more than 10,000 sold over three and a half years and between 300 and 500 moving each week during livestreams.From apartment to greenhouseAs the business expanded, the apartment could no longer keep up. In February 2026, Hurst began renting space at a family-run nursery in Los Angeles’ San Fernando Valley. The new location includes a 3,000-square-foot greenhouse and an attached house, providing much needed room for inventory, packing, and livestream sales. The move marked a major shift from a home based operation to a more established business.The team has grown from three family members to 24 employees, including Hurst’s father, his husband’s mother, longtime neighbors, and former customers. That mix reflects how the business developed organically, with people who supported Hurst early on becoming part of its future. He said the growth still feels unreal, especially when he considers that he once ran the entire operation from a balcony.For Hurst, the company has become about more than plants. Viewers have shared personal experiences involving depression, grief, and domestic violence, while some customers have become friends and stay connected through a Discord group. He believes the livestreams make people feel seen and give them a sense of belonging, which is part of why they return week after week.What comes nextHurst hopes to double the size of the business in the coming year and bring on additional livestream hosts. His advice to people hoping to turn an interest into a business is to start small, trust their instincts, and show up as themselves. He says that new sellers should approach livestreaming like talking to a friend, not like performing for a crowd.His story is proof of the fact that losing a job can sometimes open up unexpected doors. Brandon Hurst combined real hustle and real connection to build a business from one pink plant in a pink pot to a greenhouse that sells thousands of plants a week. What began as a way to pay the bills has become a family enterprise that sells more than 100,000 plants a year and brings in millions in annual sales.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient.
