articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Leader of the opposition in Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge on Saturday accused Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar of facilitating
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Leader of the opposition in Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge on Saturday accused Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar of facilitating "vote theft" and listed six charges against him at a symbolic "public impeachment" organised by the opposition INDIA bloc.Kharge alleged that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls was initiated to remove voters opposed to the BJP. The proceedings began at his residence on Rajaji Marg, with former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar chairing the event.Kharge accused the CEC of centralising control over electoral rolls and acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah.During the proceedings, Kharge listed six allegations against Kumar:Conspired to steal electionsDeleted 13.3 crore votersRewrote Form 6 without parliamentary oversight or knowledgeSeized the electoral rolls through ECINETBreached his constitutional mandate and shut out the two other election commissionersActed at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Amit ShahKharge also reiterated the opposition's three demands: The removal of the CECAn end to the SIR exerciseChanges to the 2023 law governing the appointment of the chief election commissioner.Kharge also accused PM Modi government of using various means to retain power since 2014, including defections, splitting parties, misuse of central agencies and alleged electoral irregularities."The proposal we are bringing today is to safeguard the dignity of a constitutional institution. We have no personal enmity with the CEC. Our intention is that the Election Commission should function impartially in keeping with the spirit of the Constitution. The trust of the common man in it should remain intact. No one sitting in Delhi should be able to wrongly delete the voting rights of weaker sections, women, and youth using a computer," Kharge posted on X.He further alleged that the government had repeatedly tried to retain power through various means."The Modi government has hatched every conspiracy since 2014 to cling to power: stealing MPs, breaking parties, stealing governments, Electoral Bonds, misuse of ED/CBI. And now Vote Theft—cut opposition votes and rule. There are hundreds of examples of Vote Theft," he said.Kharge also criticised the 2023 law governing the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC), alleging that it provided the election commissioner with legal protection."Gyanesh Kumar is able to carry out this theft because of the 2023 CEC Act. In December 2023, this bill was passed by suspending 145 opposition MPs. This law gives the CEC a lifelong protective shield that even the President and CJI do not have," he added.Questioning the results of the 2024 Maharashtra and Haryana assembly elections, Kharge alleged that the INDIA bloc's strong performance in the Lok Sabha elections was followed by a reversal in the state polls due to electoral irregularities."In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, we had an excellent performance in Maharashtra and Haryana, but the results flipped in the assembly elections. Reason—votes were illegally added before the elections and then all names were removed. This work is being done together by Modi-Shah and Gyanesh," he alleged.Earlier in the day, Lok Sabha leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi called on people to join a march in the national capital on Sunday ahead of the INDIA bloc's rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1.In a post on X, Rahul announced the route and timing of the walk, saying, "See you tomorrow, let's walk together."According to his post, the march will begin at noon from the Minto Road junction near Connaught Place, proceed towards Ajmeri Gate and conclude at Ramlila Maidan.However, Delhi Police sources said no permission had been sought for a march starting from Connaught Place.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Cancer, Weekly Horoscope, November 01 to November 07, 2026: Career recognition rises as family matters need patience
articles.summary: General: This week begins on a bright note for you, Cancer, almost like the first clear patch of sky after several cloudy mornings.
articles.body: General:This week begins on a bright note for you, Cancer, almost like the first clear patch of sky after several cloudy mornings. Monday brings respect, visibility, and a pleasant sense that people are listening when you speak. Business people may notice enquiries, fresh orders, or easier movement in pending matters. Still, there is a little fog inside your own mind. You may look successful from the outside while feeling oddly unsure within. That's the week's first lesson. Praise is nice, but clear thinking matters more. Don't make a big decision just because the mood around you feels encouraging.Tuesday keeps the practical momentum going. Money matters, savings, family dealings, and even difficult conversations can be handled well if you stay patient and organised. A guest may arrive, or the home may become busier than expected. Midweek changes the pace. Wednesday and Thursday push you into action. A short trip, a bold move, extra effort at work, and a need to watch your temper all come into the picture. Courage is high, but the road gets a little uneven. By Friday, you may feel slow in body yet stronger in spirit. Then Saturday becomes crowded with tasks, neighbourhood connections, and small social obligations. It's a full week, not a quiet one. You won't be bored, that's certain.Love and Relationships:Your relationships carry mixed weather this week, so timing will matter. Early in the week, your voice has unusual charm. People listen. They trust what you say. This is excellent for smoothing over old misunderstandings with relatives, in laws, or even someone who had turned cold toward you. Tuesday is especially good for rebuilding harmony with family members and settling low grade tension that has dragged on too long. If you've been meaning to call someone, apologise, or simply speak more gently, do it then. The response is likely to be better than expected.Marriage and close partnerships need extra care around Wednesday. A small argument can flare up quickly, especially if one of you feels unheard or overworked. If you're travelling, running errands, or managing too many tasks at once, impatience may spill into your tone. Slow down before replying. Thursday is kinder, and your spouse becomes more supportive again. Lovers also see a sweeter patch then, with joy, reassurance, and more warmth in communication. If you're in a new relationship, don't test the bond with unnecessary suspicion midweek. Let trust breathe.Children and younger family members bring happy moments as the week moves on. Good news from a child, progress in studies, or a simple proud moment at home can lift your heart. Saturday also brings fresh social energy. You may connect better with neighbours or meet someone new who adds a pleasant spark to your routine. An old friend may return unexpectedly too, and that meeting could stir memory, laughter, and a reminder of simpler days. Keep your heart open, but keep your voice soft. This week's relationships improve when you stop trying to control every response.Education and Career:Career and study matters are active from the very start. Monday can put you in the spotlight. If you run a business, handle clients, or work in a role where reputation matters, this is a fine beginning. Orders, requests, or opportunities may come with less struggle than usual. Still, don't let applause make you careless. Think through contracts, numbers, and timelines. For those in service, your work may attract appreciation, but you'll still need follow through to turn that into lasting gain.Tuesday is one of the stronger days for planning and strategic effort. You can persuade people with your words, settle disputes, and make headway in places where resistance had built up. Teachers, trainers, counsellors, salespeople, media workers, and anyone who relies on voice or communication can do especially well. It is also a favourable time for beginning a child's learning journey or setting a fresh academic rhythm at home. Students should use the early part of the week to organise notes, complete assignments, and ask doubts plainly instead of waiting.From Wednesday onward, effort becomes the price of progress. Short trips, unusual tasks, and sudden adjustments may demand more energy than expected. Thursday confirms that success is possible, but only if you put in extra work. Support from younger siblings or colleagues can help. Friday may make you feel lazy or mentally unsettled, yet your confidence rises, and that inner steel matters. Students can still hit their targets if they avoid distractions and keep a realistic schedule. Saturday is busy and slightly tense, so double check travel plans, reply to messages on time, and don't leave essential tasks hanging till night.Money and Finance:Financially, the week starts with promise. Monday supports gains through business, market movement, and selective speculative activity, but only if you think before acting. This is not a week for blind excitement. You may be tempted to follow a tip, copy someone else's investment choice, or make a quick decision because the atmosphere seems lucky. Stop. Count twice. Your instincts are useful now, but they need facts beside them.Tuesday is stronger for accumulation, savings, and sensible investment. If you've been planning to put money aside, open a recurring deposit, clear a dues list, or sort family finances, this is the right mood for it. The home may also see some spending because of guests or domestic needs, but that should remain manageable if planned properly. By Wednesday, finances become more average, and it would be wise to postpone any thought of buying a vehicle. The timing isn't right, and unnecessary haste could bring regret or extra cost.Thursday and Friday show that money comes through effort, not magic. Hard work pays, especially in practical fields, sales, trade, or task based work. This is also why starting a completely new venture in the latter half of the week is not ideal. Build what is already in your hand rather than chasing ten new openings. Saturday may bring small expenses through local travel, social visits, or health needs, so keep some cash aside. No dramatic money trouble appears, but discipline is your best friend this week. Spend with a cool head, not a restless one.Health and Well-being:Your health needs steady care because the week's pace rises and falls sharply. Monday feels strong overall, but mental confusion can quietly tire you more than physical work does. If you keep smiling for others while second guessing yourself inside, the body absorbs that strain. Sleep properly. Eat on time. Don't rely on tea and adrenaline to carry you through a packed day.Wednesday is the point to watch more closely. Short travel, overconfidence, and arguments can all disturb your system. If you're thinking of driving long distances or handling a vehicle related errand, delay it if possible. The day also asks you to be gentle with digestion and stamina. By Friday, a strange mix of laziness and restlessness may set in. That's usually a sign that your mind wants movement while your body wants rest. Listen carefully. You don't have to prove toughness every hour.Saturday is busy and can scatter your energy if you're not careful. Drive safely. Avoid eating out carelessly, especially oily or stale food from rushed social visits. Better to return home and eat something simple. Tension can rise from too many small interactions, neighbours, errands, old friends, one more function, one more trip. Enough. Leave room in the evening to unwind. A slow walk, lighter dinner, and less screen time will help settle the nervous system. By week's end, your well-being improves most through simple discipline, not grand fixes.Get the latest astrology news and horoscope updates. articles.body: DHARMAPURI: A case has been registered under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act against A Govindasamy, former Pappireddipatti AIADMK MLA, and others on charges of humiliating and intimidating petrol bunk employees near Dharmapuri.The complainant is R Arunkumar, 37, of Vellalapatti, who has been working at CKM Bharat Petrol Bunk in Rajapettai for the past six months. In his complaint, Arunkumar stated that Govindasamy and his accomplices, numbering more than 30, arrived at the petrol bunk around 10.45am on Oct 26.Arunkumar alleged that the former MLA obstructed vehicles entering the bunk for refuelling and verbally abused him using obscene language and caste-based slurs. Arunkumar stated that his coworker, Nandakumar, who questioned the behaviour, was also assaulted by those who accompanied the former MLA.Based on the complaint, Arunkumar approached the Dharmapuri superintendent of police A K Arun Kabilan on Friday seeking action against Govindasamy and others under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.Following an inquiry led by Dharmapuri deputy superintendent of Police Sivaraman, a case was registered against the former MLA and others at the Dharmapuri Town B-1 police station.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Coimbatore | Silver Rate in Coimbatore | Bank Holidays in Coimbatore | Public Holidays in Coimbatore | Coimbatore AQI | Weather in Coimbatore | Petrol Price in Coimbatore | Diesel Price in Coimbatore | CNG Price in Coimbatore | LPG Price in CoimbatoreStay updated with the latest Coimbatore news. articles.title: BMC's OC amnesty scheme struggles to take off as less than 10 apply in nearly 2 months; 19,000 buildings lack certificates
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Nearly 19,000 buildings in Mumbai are estimated to be functioning without Occupation Certificates (OCs), but a civic amnesty scheme intended to
articles.body: MUMBAI: Nearly 19,000 buildings in Mumbai are estimated to be functioning without Occupation Certificates (OCs), but a civic amnesty scheme intended to help eligible property owners obtain the crucial document has received fewer than 10 applications, exposing a major gap between the policy's promise and its implementation.The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) issued a standard operating procedure (SOP) for the revised OC Amnesty Scheme on September 8, offering concessions on specified regularisation charges to eligible buildings occupied before November 17, 2016.However, almost two months after its rollout, the response remains negligible.While industry estimates put the number of OC-less buildings at around 19,000, the BMC's own estimate is understood to be considerably lower, at around 4,500. The issue affects thousands of families who face higher property taxes and water charges, besides difficulties in securing housing loans, selling flats and undertaking redevelopment.With the initial six-month concession window ending on March 8, 2027, the Practising Engineers, Architects and Town Planners Association (PEATA-India) has organised a public seminar on November 3 at Yogi Sabhagrah, Dadar (East), to explain the scheme's provisions, eligibility conditions and application procedure to housing societies and individual flat owners.Who qualifies, and who does notThe scheme is not a blanket amnesty for all buildings constructed without permission.It covers eligible residential buildings, schools and hospitals that were occupied before November 17, 2016, have the prescribed development permissions, including an Intimation of Disapproval (IOD), approved plans and a Commencement Certificate (CC), but have not obtained an OC.Unauthorised buildings constructed without the requisite approvals, or unauthorised floors and extensions that fall outside the scheme's provisions, cannot claim protection under the amnesty.Eligibility and the extent of permissible regularisation will be determined by the BMC after scrutiny.The scheme also provides for individual flat owners to apply for an OC, rather than making the entire housing society's participation a prerequisite.Applications have to be submitted online through the BMC's AutoDCR system with the assistance of a registered architect or licensed surveyor. This provision could help residents where developers have disappeared, failed to complete documentation or are unwilling to pursue the OC.Costs remain a major deterrentDespite the concessions, the financial burden of regularisation remains a concern.Housing activists point out that where additional floor space index (FSI) or other permissible development rights have to be purchased to regularise eligible deviations, the premium can run into lakhs of rupees.In some cases, individual flat owners could face an outlay of Rs 10 lakh to Rs 20 lakh, depending on the location and nature of the deviation.This raises concerns about residents having to bear the financial consequences of deviations or procedural defaults committed by developers. Societies are also uncertain about how the costs and liabilities should be apportioned among flat owners.Another source of confusion is the distinction between obtaining an OC and regularising unauthorised construction.The amnesty provides a route to address specified deviations and procedural shortcomings in otherwise sanctioned buildings; it does not confer blanket legality on all existing construction.What the revised SOP offersThe SOP provides a graded concession on penalties linked to eligible FSI regularisation.Applications received during the first six months from September 8, 2026, are eligible for a 100% waiver of the applicable penalty.Applications received between six and 12 months are eligible for a 50% concession on the prevailing penalty, while applications after the first year will attract the full applicable penalty.The procedure also provides a 50% concession on specified regularisation charges for eligible balcony, otla and loft enclosures and other covered deviations.Additional FSI and fungible compensatory area concessions are also prescribed for qualifying residential tenements, subject to the scheme's conditions.For redevelopment projects, the SOP provides for the rehabilitation component's OC to be delinked from violations in the sale component, subject to the prescribed approval.This could prevent eligible rehabilitation buildings from being held up solely because of compliance issues in the sale wing.The concessions, however, do not dispense with mandatory safety and statutory requirements. Applicants must meet the applicable fire-safety, lift and other clearance conditions, wherever required."Countless Mumbaikars are living in buildings without OCs because of historical bottlenecks. Many do not realise that the state government and civic body have provided an opportunity to address these issues with substantial concessions," said PEATA-India president Yomesh Rao."Our objective at the November 3 seminar is to explain the documentation and application process so that housing societies and individual flat owners understand the provisions and do not lose out on the concession period," he said.Seminar details:PEATA-India's seminar on decoding the BMC's OC Amnesty Scheme and SOP will be held on November 3, 2026, from 5pm onwards at Yogi Sabhagriha, Dadar (East).Society managing committee members, flat owners, developers, architects and surveyors are expected to attend.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: Cops seize 83kg ganja hidden in tractor
articles.summary: Sambalpur police seized 83 kg ganja hidden in a special compartment under a tractor trolley; driver fled during chase and investigation is ongoing.
articles.body: Sambalpur: Nakti Deul police seized an unregistered red tractor carrying around 83 kg of ganja packed in four gunny bags and concealed in a specially built compartment beneath its trolley on Saturday. Acting on the tip-off, a special police team launched a search around 1.40 pm, said additional SP Ajay Kumar Mishra.The tractor was going from Mushakani village towards Batgaon when police started following it. Sensing the chase, the driver left the tractor in a forest near Telisingha chowk and fled. Police searched the area but could not find him. Efforts are on to identify the owner and driver.
